title: Special Episode: What Does It Mean to 'Never Forget'?

sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross-Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 你好，我是安德鲁·罗斯-索尔金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for DealBook, a daily newsletter at the New York Times.
sentences.zh: 我为《纽约时报》的每日通讯《DealBook》报道商业和政策新闻。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市举行的DealBook峰会上现场采访一些商业、政治和文化领域最具影响力的人物，包括J.D.

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk, Christine Lagarde, Zilran Mondani, and many others, live on stage at the DealBook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、克里斯蒂娜·拉加德、齐尔兰·蒙达尼等多人。

sentences.en: You can watch some of these unguarded, unfiltered conversations as they happen.
sentences.zh: 你可以实时观看其中一些毫无防备、未经剪辑的对话。

sentences.en: We're going to be live-streaming select interviews for anyone to watch, free, at nytimes.com on November 18th.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我们将在nytimes.com上直播部分精选采访，供所有人免费观看。

sentences.en: If you're not already a subscriber, you can download the New York Times app to watch and get a month of free access to all of our journalism.
sentences.zh: 如果你还不是订阅用户，可以下载《纽约时报》应用程序进行观看，并获得我们所有新闻内容一个月的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 希望你能收看。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 你一定不想错过。

sentences.en: Hi, I'm Dan Barry, a writer for the New York Times.
sentences.zh: 你好，我是丹·巴里，《纽约时报》的一名撰稿人。

sentences.en: Here's my personal essay, What Does It Mean to Never Forget 9-11?
sentences.zh: 这是我的个人随笔：《“永志不忘”9·11意味着什么？》

sentences.en: In his mind, Michael Regan should have been down there.
sentences.zh: 在他心里，迈克尔·里根当时本该在那儿。

sentences.en: He should have had the guts.
sentences.zh: 他本该有那个胆量。

sentences.en: A longtime New York City employee who became first deputy fire commissioner after the terrorist attacks of September 11th, 2001,
sentences.zh: 作为一名在纽约市工作多年的老员工，他在2001年9月11日恐怖袭击后担任了第一副消防局长，

sentences.en: Mr. Regan coordinated scores of funerals and memorial services and helped hundreds of shattered families.
sentences.zh: 里根先生协调了数十场葬礼和追悼会，并帮助了数百个支离破碎的家庭。

sentences.en: Still, he could not shake the guilt.
sentences.zh: 尽管如此，他还是无法摆脱内心的愧疚。

sentences.en: He should have been there, down at the World Trade Center.
sentences.zh: 他本该在那儿，在世贸中心现场。

sentences.en: After a couple of months, Mr. Regan finally shared his remorse with a stunned fire department colleague who told him that he had been there.
sentences.zh: 几个月后，里根先生终于向一位目瞪口呆的消防局同事倾诉了他的悔恨，而那位同事告诉他，他其实去过现场。

sentences.en: He'd helped transport the bodies of the first deputy fire commissioner, Bill Thien, and the chief of department, Peter Ganty, to the morgue on First Avenue.
sentences.zh: 他曾协助将第一副消防局长比尔·蒂恩和部门主管彼得·甘蒂的遗体运送到第一大道的停尸房。

sentences.en: Don't you remember?
sentences.zh: 你不记得了吗？

sentences.en: Looking back, Mr. Regan said his mental block must have been a way to cope with the instant loss of thousands, including many close friends.
sentences.zh: 回首往事，里根先生说，他的心理阻滞一定是一种应对瞬间失去数千人（包括许多挚友）的方式。

sentences.en: It was a safety mechanism, he said.
sentences.zh: 他说，这是一种防御机制。

sentences.en: I saw horrible things that day, and I didn't want to think about those things.
sentences.zh: 那天我看到了可怕的事情，我不想去想那些事情。

sentences.en: Twenty years later, the command to never forget retains its power,
sentences.zh: 二十年后，“永志不忘”的口号依然具有力量，

sentences.en: jolting us into the past whenever we see it on a hat or flag or the back of a passing car on the belt parkway.
sentences.zh: 每当我们在帽子、旗帜或腰带公园大道上行驶的汽车后窗上看到它时，它都会把我们拉回过去。

sentences.en: For all its slogan-like simplicity, these twinned words seem freighted with the complexities of guilt, obligation, and even presumption, as if we could ever forget.
sentences.zh: 尽管这句口号听起来很简单，但这两个词似乎承载着内疚、义务甚至自以为是的复杂含义，仿佛我们真的能忘记一样。

sentences.en: But now that an entire generation has been born since the day, versions of the question posed to Mr. Regan might be asked of all of us who lived it in some way.
sentences.zh: 但现在，距离那一天已经过去了一整代人，对于我们这些以某种方式亲历过那一天的人来说，里根先生所面临的问题，或许也同样适用于我们所有人。

sentences.en: Two planes hijacked by al-Qaeda piercing the north and south towers of the World Trade Center.
sentences.zh: 两架被基地组织劫持的飞机撞向了世贸中心的北塔和南塔。

sentences.en: A third slamming into the Pentagon in Arlington, Virginia.
sentences.zh: 第三架撞向了弗吉尼亚州阿灵顿的五角大楼。

sentences.en: A fourth crashing in an open field outside Shanksville, Pennsylvania.
sentences.zh: 第四架坠毁在宾夕法尼亚州尚克斯维尔外的一片开阔地上。

sentences.en: All in less than 90 minutes.
sentences.zh: 这一切都发生在不到90分钟内。

sentences.en: What exactly do you remember?
sentences.zh: 你到底记得什么？

sentences.en: What stories do you tell when a casual conversation morphs into a therapy session?
sentences.zh: 当随意的谈话演变成心理治疗时，你会讲述什么样的故事？

sentences.en: What stories do you keep to yourself?
sentences.zh: 你又会把什么样的故事藏在心里？

sentences.en: And what instantly transports you back to that deceptively sunny Tuesday morning?
sentences.zh: 又是什么瞬间把你带回了那个看似阳光明媚的周二早晨？

sentences.en: For Nikki Stern, a writer, it might be the waft of cigar smoke.
sentences.zh: 对于作家妮基·斯特恩来说，那可能是雪茄烟的味道。

sentences.en: Her husband, Jim Petorti, a vice president at Martian McLennan, who worked on the 96th floor of the North Tower, enjoyed the occasional cigar.
sentences.zh: 她的丈夫吉姆·佩托蒂是马什·麦克伦南公司的一名副总裁，在北塔96楼工作，他偶尔喜欢抽雪茄。

sentences.en: Or it might be the sight of a bicycle.
sentences.zh: 或者可能是一辆自行车的景象。

sentences.en: Just a bicycle.
sentences.zh: 仅仅是一辆自行车。

sentences.en: Jim used to cycle.
sentences.zh: 吉姆以前常骑自行车。

sentences.en: I compartmentalize, Ms. Stern said.
sentences.zh: “我把记忆分门别类地存放，”斯特恩女士说。

sentences.en: But there's a permanent leak in the compartment.
sentences.zh: “但那个隔间里有一个永远修不好的漏洞。”

sentences.en: For James Luongo, a former deputy chief of the New York Police Department, it's driving past the now-closed Fresh Kills landfill on Staten Island.
sentences.zh: 对于前纽约警察局副局长詹姆斯·卢昂戈来说，那是开车经过斯塔滕岛上现已关闭的弗雷什基尔斯垃圾填埋场。

sentences.en: He spent nearly a year on that mound, supervising a pop-up base camp where 1.8 million tons of trade-centered debris were sifted for human remains and personal effects.
sentences.zh: 他在那座土堆上待了近一年，监管着一个临时基地，那里有180万吨世贸中心的残骸被筛查，以寻找人类遗骸和个人物品。

sentences.en: The problem is, Mr. Luongo lives on Staten Island.
sentences.zh: 问题是，卢昂戈先生就住在斯塔滕岛。

sentences.en: You've got to put it where it needs to be, he said of the memories, and not open the door more than you have to.
sentences.zh: 谈到这些记忆时，他说：“你必须把它们放在该放的地方，不要在不必要的时候打开那扇门。”

sentences.en: Never forget.
sentences.zh: 永志不忘。

sentences.en: When I hear never forget for 9-11, my next question is, never forget what, said Charles B.
sentences.zh: “当我听到‘永志不忘’9·11时，我的下一个问题是，‘永不忘记什么？’”约翰·杰伊刑事司法学院心理学副教授查尔斯·B·斯通说。

sentences.en: Stone, an associate professor of psychology at John Jay College of Criminal Justice.
sentences.zh: “永不忘记导致这一切的国际局势，随之而来的国土不安全感，包括仅仅因为是穆斯林而遭受骚扰的美国公民，

sentences.en: Never forget the international dynamics that set the stage, the homeland insecurities that followed, including the harassment of American citizens for simply being Muslim,
sentences.zh: 那几个月里似乎永无止境的葬礼，以及二十年的战争与流血。”

sentences.en: the months of seemingly non-stop funerals, the two decades of war and bloodshed.
sentences.zh: “最接近的答案可能是，永不忘记它曾经发生过，”斯通先生说。

sentences.en: Probably the closest answer is, never forget that it occurred, Mr. Stone said.
sentences.zh: 但那些细枝末节终将被遗忘。

sentences.en: But it's the little details that will be forgotten.
sentences.zh: 我记得。

sentences.en: I remember.
sentences.zh: 当另一具遗体从废墟中被拉出，在人们的敬礼和放在胸前的建筑工头盔中被抬走时，那种寂静。

sentences.en: The stillness as another body was pulled from the rubble and carted away to salutes and construction helmets held over hearts.
sentences.zh: 停尸房外冷藏车发出的嗡嗡声。

sentences.en: The hum of the refrigerated trucks outside the morgue.
sentences.zh: 那种痛苦的辛辣气味，穿过新闻编辑室敞开的窗户飘向住宅区。

sentences.en: The acrid smell of loss drifting uptown through the newsroom's open windows.
sentences.zh: 垃圾填埋场。

sentences.en: The landfill.
sentences.zh: 葬礼。

sentences.en: The funerals.
sentences.zh: 尘埃。

sentences.en: The duSt.
sentences.zh: 当然，“永志不忘”的呼吁也可以被解读为另一种值得尊敬的尝试，旨在保留那天多种情绪的一丝痕迹。

sentences.en: Of course, the call to never forget can also be interpreted as another honorable attempt to preserve some faint sense of the day's many emotions.
sentences.zh: 值得尊敬，但在岁月无情的磨损和记忆的变幻莫测面前，或许是徒劳的。

sentences.en: Honorable, but perhaps futile against the ceaseless rub of the passing years, the vagaries of memory.
sentences.zh: 在9·11袭击发生后的最初几天，全国各地的学者团队着手捕捉那一刻的“闪光灯记忆”。

sentences.en: In the first days after the September 11th attacks, a team of scholars around the country set out to capture the moment's flashbulb memories.
sentences.zh: 这是在历史重大事件发生瞬间形成的生动、持久的心理快照，例如珍珠港事件或约翰·F·肯尼迪遇刺。

sentences.en: The vivid, enduring mental snapshots formed at the instant of historical import, such as the bombing of Pearl Harbor or the assassination of John F.
sentences.zh: 他们问了3000多人几个问题，包括：当你得知恐怖袭击时，你在哪里？

sentences.en: Kennedy.
sentences.zh: 在纽约，参与这项研究的研究生们在联合广场和华盛顿广场摆设摊位并分发问卷，

sentences.en: They asked more than 3,000 people a few questions, including, where were you when you learned about the terrorist attacks?
sentences.zh: 袭击发生后的几天和几周里，成千上万的人聚集在那里，只是为了陪伴彼此。

sentences.en: In New York, graduate students working on the study set up tables and handed out surveys at Union Square and Washington Square,
sentences.zh: 那种共同哀悼的时刻现在也正在从记忆中滑落。

sentences.en: where thousands had gathered in the days and weeks after the attacks just to be with one another.
sentences.zh: 一年后，研究人员向许多相同的人提出了同样的问题，结果发现40%的记忆已经改变了。

sentences.en: Moments of communal mourning also now slipping from memory.
sentences.zh: 一个现在说他在得知袭击时在办公室的人，之前可能曾说他当时在火车上。

sentences.en: A year later, the researchers asked the same questions of many of the same people, only to find that 40% of the memories had changed.
sentences.zh: 哈佛大学神经科学教授、参与了9·11记忆研究的伊丽莎白·A·菲尔普斯表示，这些改变了的记忆与针对其他历史事件进行的类似研究结果是一致的。

sentences.en: A man now saying that he was in the office when he learned of the attacks might previously have said that he had been on a train.
sentences.zh: 与普通的自传体记忆相比，9·11记忆的独特之处在于人们对自己改变了的记忆产生了极大的自信，

sentences.en: These altered recollections were consistent with similar studies done in connection with other historical events, according to Elizabeth A.
sentences.zh: 这种自信在周年纪念日时已经开始固化。

sentences.en: Phelps, a professor of neuroscience at Harvard University, who worked on the 9-11 memory study.
sentences.zh: “你有你的故事，并且坚持这个版本，”菲尔普斯博士说。

sentences.en: What distinguished the memories of September 11th when compared with ordinary autobiographical memories was the extreme confidence that people had developed in their altered remembrances,
sentences.zh: 新学院社会研究中心心理学教授威廉·赫斯特也参与了这项研究，他表示赞同。

sentences.en: which by the first anniversary had begun to concretize.
sentences.zh: “我认为发生的情况是，他们围绕自己的‘闪光灯记忆’构建了一个叙事，”他说。

sentences.en: You have your story, and you're sticking to it, Dr. Phelps said.
sentences.zh: “这成了他们的故事。”

sentences.en: William Hurst, a professor of psychology at the New School for Social Research, who also worked on the study, agreed.
sentences.zh: 赫斯特博士想知道记忆的变化是否与某种身份认同感有关。

sentences.en: I think what happens is they develop a narrative about their flashbulb memory, he said.
sentences.zh: 毕竟，如果你不知道自己第一次听说9·11袭击是什么时候，作为一个纽约人，这说明了什么？

sentences.en: It becomes their story.
sentences.zh: 作为一个美国人，这又说明了什么？

sentences.en: Dr. Hurst wonders whether the changes in memory are somehow linked to a sense of identity.
sentences.zh: 将个人叙事与历史上的重大时刻对齐，可能是一种宣示你属于受影响群体、你属于这里的方式。

sentences.en: After all, what would it say about you as a New Yorker?
sentences.zh: 不可避免地，总有一天，世上将不再有人拥有关于9·11的个人叙事。

sentences.en: As an American, if you didn't know how you first heard about the September 11th attacks?
sentences.zh: 不可避免地，随着时间的推移，将生动的亲身经历转化为枯燥的历史课，那天的情感冲击会一点点消退，然后消退得更多。

sentences.en: Aligning one's personal narrative with a consequential moment in history may be a way of asserting that you were a part of the affected community, that you belong.
sentences.zh: 这种转变已经开始了。

sentences.en: Inevitably, someday there will be no one alive with a personal narrative of September 11th.
sentences.zh: 问问任何一位高中历史老师就知道了。

sentences.en: Inevitably, the emotional impact of the day will fade a little bit, and then a little bit more, as time transforms a visceral lived experience into a dry history lesson.
sentences.zh: 但就目前而言，对许多人来说，9·11仍然是一种亲身经历。

sentences.en: This transformation has already begun.
sentences.zh: 我们有自己的故事，有我们可能已经改变了的记忆，可以在周年纪念日或一年中的任何一天分享，也可以选择不分享。

sentences.en: Ask any high school history teacher.
sentences.zh: 我们讲述故事可能是为了抵御时间不可避免的抹除。

sentences.en: But for now, for many, September 11th remains a lived experience.
sentences.zh: 我们讲述它们可能是为了帮助我们消化那一刻，或者解释为什么每当我们听到布鲁斯·斯普林斯汀的《The Rising》时，我们都会变得沉默。

sentences.en: We have our stories, our possibly altered memories, to share or not to share on the anniversary or any day of the year.
sentences.zh: 又或者，我们可能把故事锁在某个有漏洞的隔间里，生怕被视为另一个9·11自恋者，也就是我们自己叙事中的英雄。

sentences.en: We might tell our stories to hold back the inevitable erasure of time.
sentences.zh: 又或者，我们出于单纯的敬畏而将它们藏在心里。

sentences.en: We might tell them to help us process the moment or to explain why we grow quiet whenever we hear Bruce Springsteen's The Rising.
sentences.zh: 里根先生，那个曾经短暂遗忘的人，现在64岁，是摩根大通的一名高管。

sentences.en: Then again, we might keep our stories locked in some leaky compartment for fear of being perceived as another 9-11 narcissist, the hero of our own narrative.
sentences.zh: 他有他的记忆，他的故事。

sentences.en: Or maybe we keep them to ourselves out of simple reverence.
sentences.zh: 有些故事以那种爱尔兰式的黑色幽默方式显得很有趣。

sentences.en: Mr. Regan, the man who momentarily forgot, is now 64 and an executive with J.P.
sentences.zh: 有些则令人清醒到只能以沉默回应。

sentences.en: Morgan Chase.
sentences.zh: 他避开周年纪念日、每年对死者名字的诵读，以及这一天不断激发的各种纪录片、书籍和文章。

sentences.en: He has his memories, his stories.
sentences.zh: 他说，他永远不会去参观9·11纪念馆和博物馆。

sentences.en: Some are funny in that dark Irish way of coping.
sentences.zh: “我不需要回去。”

sentences.en: Some are so sobering that silence is the only response.
sentences.zh: 卢昂戈先生现年63岁，在纽约警察局工作40年后于3月退休，他的职业生涯因在斯塔滕岛垃圾填埋场度过的那许多个月而显得与众不同。

sentences.en: He avoids the anniversaries, the annual recitation of the names of the dead, and all the documentaries and books and essays the day continues to inspire.
sentences.zh: 那里回收了超过4200具人类遗骸，以及近6万件个人物品，包括照片和身份证件。

sentences.en: He will never visit the 9-11 memorial and museum, he said.
sentences.zh: 他所监管的是一个建立在悲剧之上的村庄，夜晚闪烁着微光，有办公拖车、去污中心、食堂，

sentences.en: I don't need to go back.
sentences.zh: 还有等待接收从曼哈顿下城驳运来的残骸的传送带。

sentences.en: Mr. Luongo, now 63, retired in March after 40 years with the NYPD, a career distinguished in part by those many months on the Staten Island landfill.
sentences.zh: 成堆的被压扁的车辆，包括警车和消防车，整齐而恐怖地排列着。

sentences.en: More than 4,200 human remains were recovered, as well as nearly 60,000 personal items, including photographs and identification cards.
sentences.zh: 一切都消失了，就像布里加登一样。

sentences.en: What he supervised was a village built on tragedy and a glow at night, with office trailers, a decontamination center, a mess hall,
sentences.zh: 这一切是真的吗？

sentences.en: and conveyor belts waiting to receive the debris barged from lower Manhattan.
sentences.zh: 还是说，这也是记忆的戏法？

sentences.en: Looming stacks of crushed vehicles, including police cars and fire engines, arranged in neat, horrific rows.
sentences.zh: “我记得，”卢昂戈先生说。

sentences.en: All gone, like Brigadoon.
sentences.zh: “所以你早上起床，点上一支蜡烛，做一个祈祷，然后继续生活。”

sentences.en: Was it even real?
sentences.zh: 斯特恩女士后来写了两本非虚构类书籍和四部小说，她也记得。

sentences.en: Or is this, too, a trick of memory?
sentences.zh: 她怎么可能不记得？

sentences.en: I remember, Mr. Luongo said.
sentences.zh: 在新泽西州普林斯顿家附近的超市买鸡蛋，打算为丈夫烤巧克力曲奇，

sentences.en: So you'd get up in the morning, light a candle, say a prayer, and move on.
sentences.zh: “我烤的曲奇是世界上最好吃的，”当有人喊出类似“世贸中心被撞了”的话时。

sentences.en: Ms. Stern, who went on to write two nonfiction books and four novels, also remembers.
sentences.zh: 六个月后接到通知，说吉姆的一块硬币大小的遗骸已被确认，

sentences.en: How could she not?
sentences.zh: 她在悲痛中每晚不停地写作，写下了超过15万字，这些文字永远不会有其他人看到。

sentences.en: Shopping for eggs in a super-fresh market near her home in Princeton, New Jersey, planning to make chocolate chip cookies for her husband,
